hints.title: In-Place Duplicate Compaction Obstacle
hints.text: Removing elements by shifting the remainder leftward on each duplicate requires quadratic work. Because equal values appear contiguously in sorted order, how can you overwrite duplicates in a single pass without extra allocations?

hints.title: Slow Writer Fast Reader Separation
hints.text: Maintain an index tracking where the next unique value belongs. Advance a reading index through the collection, copying elements forward only when an observed value differs from its predecessor.

hints.title: Single Pass Array Rewriting Procedure
hints.text: If the array is empty, return zero. Initialize a write pointer to one. Loop a read pointer from index one to the end of the array. Whenever the value at the read index does not equal the preceding value, assign it to the write position and increment the write pointer. Return the write index.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of input array (1 <= N <= 3 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass in-place array compaction using constant auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Deleting duplicate elements with array shift operations (e.g. del or splice) takes O(N) per deletion, scaling to O(N^2) total time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Overwriting elements in-place with a slow-fast pointer pattern achieves optimal O(N) time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Overwriting elements in-place without auxiliary arrays, maintaining the relative order of elements, and returning the correct length k.
